sections.overview: Catoptria verellus is a small European grass-veneer moth in the family Crambidae, known in French as crambus enfumé.
sections.identification: Its wingspan is about 17–18 mm; the forewings are brown with pale markings, giving a marbled appearance.
sections.habitat: It occurs in varied European habitats; larvae are associated with mosses growing on tree trunks.
sections.diet: The caterpillars feed on mosses, including those growing on apple, plum and poplar trees.
sections.behavior: Adults come to light and are recorded mainly in early summer, with later flight possible in mild weather.
sections.reproduction: Larvae develop on moss substrates; detailed species-specific egg and pupal timing is not established by the accounts consulted.
sections.ecology: It belongs to Catoptria, a genus of grass-veneer moths; the related C. pinella is another European congener but its larvae use different plant substrates.
sections.conservation: No species-specific conservation assessment was located; the Belgian catalogue describes it as common there, which does not establish status across its full range.
